claims.text: The starting TiZrHfNb alloy is single-phase, compositionally uniform, and structurally well characterized.
Nb will be progressively replaced by V over a 0% to 20% substitution range while synthesis and homogenization conditions are held constant.
Replacing Nb with V changes the alloy's valence electron concentration.
The change in valence electron concentration caused by V substitution systematically modifies the density of states near the Fermi level.
Changes in the density of states at the Fermi level alter the electron-phonon coupling strength.
Electron-phonon coupling mediates Cooper pairing in the proposed BCS-type superconducting state.
Tc varies non-monotonically with V substitution and reaches a maximum at an intermediate V level.
An intermediate V concentration produces a significantly higher Tc than the 0% V baseline.
V concentrations below and above the optimum produce lower Tc values than the optimum.
Specific-heat coefficients change with V substitution in a manner consistent with changes in the Fermi-level density of states.
The electronic specific-heat coefficient can be used to estimate the conduction-electron density of states at the Fermi level.
Identical processing plus XRD, SEM, TEM, and EDS verification can isolate electron-count tuning from phase separation and significant microstructural changes.
Conventional BCS-like superconductivity with appreciable electron-phonon coupling occurs in at least a subset of superconducting high-entropy alloys.
The proposed mechanism applies only while the alloy remains single-phase and is not dominated by competing structural-disorder effects.
V substitution beyond approximately 20%, or any condition producing secondary phases or major microstructural changes, is outside the hypothesis's boundary.
Compositional disorder can suppress superconductivity in some HEAs but may enhance Tc under other conditions.
Superconducting transition temperature in HEAs depends on chemical composition.
The unmodified 0% V TiZrHfNb alloy processed identically is the experimental baseline.
Failure to observe a non-monotonic Tc trend with an intermediate composition significantly above the baseline would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The boundary declares samples with secondary phases or significant microstructural changes to be outside the hypothesis, whereas the falsification rule says occurrence of those same changes would falsify the hypothesis. An out-of-domain experiment cannot by itself decisively falsify the in-domain mechanism.
